chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Duke or Fletcher: the best big band of 1928-33
summary: Asked which band was the best, Butler says it was a toss-up between Ellington and Henderson, with Chick Webb also fine.

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you something previous to that, the first few years you were in New York, 1928 to 1933, five years, before you went -- okay, you came in the middle of '28, you were going to Germany in the middle of '33, right? Five years.
'32 or '33. Four or five years, yeah.
'33. Amongst the guys of the bands you were in at that time, who's band was considered the best of the big bands?

Well, it was a toss-up between Duke and Fletcher. You see, Fletcher had a stomp band, see, Fletcher and they would battle had a stomp band and Fletcher would come up there/every year, you know. Chick Webb had a beautiful band but Fletcher and Duke, they was the kings. They was the kings.
